review_notes:
I read the whole target file and compared it with Selector.lean, Gates.lean and GateCoefficients.lean in the same directory. Two repetition patterns stood out.

1. The identity `monomial (edgeExponent (i,j)) r = C r * X (.inl i) * X (.inr j)` is reproved in `selectorSplit_base`, once as `hm` and again as `hx`. The same proof also appears in `edgeProduct_nested`, `coeff_graph_edges` and two places in Gates.lean (about five copies in all).
2. The identity `allOnes (A ⊕ B) = (allOnes A).sumElim (allOnes B)` is reproved in `selectorSplit_coeff` and `permanent_block_diagonal`, and again elsewhere.

`Gates.allOnes_sum` exists, but it is stated for `Gates.allOnes`, a separate definition from `Selector.allOnes`. It cannot be used directly here.

Both patterns have short proofs, so the benefit is mainly maintenance. I did not find larger duplicated reasoning. The `rename_inner` / `rename_outer` pair is structurally parallel but each is a three-line induction, so I did not report it. I could not run Lean, so the proposed lemmas are untested. The first lemma's variable and typeclass context must match what Selector.lean declares for `edgeExponent` (type variable `n`, `[Fintype n]`), which I did not fully confirm.

findings.problem: Inside this one proof, `hm` (general `i j r`) is proved and then `hx` re-proves the same identity for `M i j` with an identical script instead of using `hm i j (M i j)`. The same identity is also reproved as a local `hm` in Selector.lean (`edgeProduct_nested`, `coeff_graph_edges`), in Gates.lean (lines 164, 215, 284), and in a variant in GateCoefficients.lean (`full_gate_split`). Each copy restates the single-edge monomial = C * X * X fact and its rewrite script.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma next to `edgeExponent` in Selector.lean:
`theorem monomial_edgeExponent {n R} [CommSemiring R] (i j : n) (r : R) : monomial (edgeExponent (i,j)) r = C r * X (.inl i) * X (.inr j)`.
Proof: the existing script `rw [C_mul_X_eq_monomial, X, monomial_mul_monomial]; simp only [edgeExponent, mul_one]`.
In `selectorSplit_base`, replace both `hm` and `hx` with it: the `simp only [baseEdges, hm, ...]` call becomes `simp only [baseEdges, monomial_edgeExponent, ...]`, and `hx` becomes `rw [monomial_edgeExponent, map_mul, map_mul]`. The other sites change the same way. The binders must match those used for `edgeExponent` in Selector.lean.
findings.benefit: The identity is proved once and named. Readers no longer have to re-check five near-identical local proofs. A future change to `edgeExponent` needs one edit instead of five. This file also loses the redundant `hx` block.

findings.problem: Both `selectorSplit_coeff` (lines 84-86, `ho`, then `rw [ho, coeff_nested]`) and `permanent_block_diagonal` (lines 231-233, `hones`, then `rw [hones, coeff_nested, ...]`) prove `allOnes (X ⊕ Y) = (allOnes X).sumElim (allOnes Y)` with `ext; cases; rfl`. This is followed by the same `coeff_nested` rewrite. The same pair also occurs in Selector.lean (`row_product_permanent`, `coeff_graph_edges`) and Gates.lean (line 244). `Gates.allOnes_sum` states this fact, but for `Gates.allOnes`, which is a different definition from `Selector.allOnes`, so none of these sites can use it.
findings.proposed_change: In Selector.lean, next to `allOnes`, add `theorem allOnes_sum {A B : Type*} [Fintype A] [Fintype B] : allOnes (A ⊕ B) = (allOnes A).sumElim (allOnes B) := by ext v; cases v <;> rfl`, and optionally a corollary `coeff_allOnes_nested p : p.coeff (allOnes (A ⊕ B)) = ((sumRingEquiv R A B p).coeff (allOnes A)).coeff (allOnes B)` obtained by `rw [allOnes_sum, coeff_nested]`. Then `selectorSplit_coeff` uses `rw [allOnes_sum, coeff_nested]` in place of `ho` (the `SelectorGateVars` side keeps the same shape), and `permanent_block_diagonal` uses `rw [allOnes_sum, coeff_nested, ...]` in place of `hones`. Ideally `Gates.allOnes` is unified with `Selector.allOnes`, so the existing `Gates.allOnes_sum` also serves these sites.
findings.benefit: This removes five or more copies of the same exponent-splitting step. It makes explicit that the proofs share one 'coefficient of an all-ones monomial in a sum-indexed polynomial' reduction. Because `Gates.allOnes` and `Selector.allOnes` are two separate definitions, it also surfaces a maintenance hazard. This gain is modest, because each copy is only one line.
